Il devrait être bâti sur le site de Mirapolis, un parc s'inspirant des contes et légendes françaises ouvert en 1987, mais qui a dû fermer ses portes quatre ans plus tard, en raison d'une fréquentation inférieure aux attentes.

item.title: USA nehmen Handelsfirma Wellbred wegen Iran-Kontakten ins Visier
item.description: Die USA haben neue Sanktionen gegen die in Singapur ansässige Firma Wellbred Capital und deren Tochtergesellschaften verhängt. Wellbred stehe mit dem iranischen Öl-Reeder Mohammad Hossein Schamchani in Verbindung, begründete das US-Finanzministerium seine Entscheidung. Die Maßnahmen richteten sich zudem gegen Handelsfirmen von Wellbred in den Vereinigten Arabischen Emiraten und der Schweiz sowie eine französische Raffinerie. Wellbred war für eine Stellungnahme zunächst nicht zu erreichen.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Die USA haben neue Sanktionen gegen die in Singapur ansässige Firma Wellbred Capital und deren Tochtergesellschaften verhängt. Wellbred stehe mit dem iranischen Öl-Reeder Mohammad Hossein Schamchani in Verbindung, begründete das US-Finanzministerium seine Entscheidung. Die Maßnahmen richteten sich zudem gegen Handelsfirmen von Wellbred in den Vereinigten Arabischen Emiraten und der Schweiz sowie eine französische Raffinerie. Wellbred war für eine Stellungnahme zunächst nicht zu erreichen. Schamchani ist der Sohn des verstorbenen hochrangigen iranischen Sicherheitsbeamten Ali Schamchani. Sein Schifffahrtsnetzwerk, das bereits in den Jahren 2025 und 2026 mit Sanktionen belegt wurde, transportiert dem Ministerium zufolge Öl aus dem Iran und Russland an Käufer weltweit. Wellbred hat seinen Hauptsitz in Singapur. Das Unternehmen handelt mit Öl, Naphtha, Petrochemikalien sowie Flüssiggas (LPG) und unterhält Niederlassungen in den Vereinigten Arabischen Emiraten, der Schweiz, Saudi-Arabien und Nigeria.

item.title: Shein's up to $1.8 billion Hong Kong IPO order book covered, sources say
item.description: Online fast-fashion retailer Shein's Hong Kong IPO book to raise up to $1.8 billion has been fully covered by investor demand, two sources said, bringing it closer to its long-awaited market debut amid growing business and regulatory challenges.
item.dc:creator: Scott Murdoch, Kane Wu
item.content:encoded: Online fast-fashion retailer Shein's Hong Kong IPO book to raise up to $1.8 billion has been fully covered by investor demand, two sources said, bringing it closer to its long-awaited market debut amid growing business and regulatory challenges. Shein launched its new share [USN:L1N44K04U TEXT:"sale"] on Monday, valuing the company at up to $27 billion. Investor orders for the offering have come from a number of existing shareholders, China-focused and multi-strategy funds, said the sources with knowledge of the matter. They declined to be named as they were not authorised to speak to the media. A spokesperson for Shein did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. The Singapore-based, Chinese-founded company is selling 280 million shares at HK$47.60 to HK$49.50 a share in the IPO, according to the company's filings, which would raise $1.8 billion at the top end. The final price of the shares is due to be unveiled on Monday and the stock is scheduled to begin trading on Hong Kong's stock exchange on September 1, according to the company filings. Shein's valuation in the IPO is a drop in excess of 70% compared to the nearly $100 billion private-market valuation that it reached in 2022. The company is best known for selling $5 dresses and $10 jeans to shoppers in about 160 countries. Analysts [USN:L6N4470JX TEXT:"said"] growing [USN:L1N44L05D TEXT:"headwinds"] in Shein's core markets — the U.S. and Europe — could weigh on the company's growth prospects. Shein's IPO comes as the company works to address environmental, social and governance [USN:L6N44E0TG TEXT:"concerns"] that have triggered regulatory investigations and fines in several countries, complicating previous [USN:L1N44L00S TEXT:"attempts"] to list its shares. Over the past four years, the company tried to list in New York and London, but faced investor and political criticism over its environmental, labour and governance standards. Shein is under investigation by the European Commission and the U.S. Federal Trade Commission. Previous probes resulted in fines in France over alleged fake discounts and in Italy over greenwashing as fast-fashion purveyors come under increased scrutiny from regulators. Greenwashing refers to the practice of overstating the environmental benefits of an organisation. A Shein spokesperson said the firm maintained "high standards of corporate governance, transparency and accountability." The filings showed Shein has locked in cornerstone investors led by existing shareholders Boyu, Tiger Global and General Atlantic to buy about $383 million worth of shares.

item.title: ブロードコムの信用リスク上昇、AI資金調達で巨額の保証提供を不安視
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 米半導体大手ブロードコムが、AIインフラ向けの巨額の資金パッケージで保証を提供する状況を受け、債券トレーダーは同社に関係する信用リスクの評価を厳しくしている。

同社の2031年満期社債（表面利率5.15%）利回りは、8月に入り約14ベーシスポイント（bp、1bp＝0.01%）上昇した。社債のデフォルト（債務不履行）に備える保証コスト、5年物クレジット・デフォルト・スワップ（CDS）スプレッド（保険料率）はこの間、28bp高くなった。オラクルやスペースXと比べても上昇率はより大きい。

ブロードコムは、アンソロピックなどの利用を想定し、AI半導体チップの資金調達ディールで600億ドル（約9兆5500億円）強の借り入れを目指し、貸し手グループと協議している。調整が続いているが、ブロードコムは担保付シニアトランシェを一部保証する可能性がある。

米投資会社アポロ・グローバル・マネジメントとブラックストーンは今年に入り、ブロードコムとアンソロピック向けに総額350億ドルのAIインフラ関連の資金パッケージをアレンジした。多くの部分の支払いをブロードコムが保証する。

借り手の特別目的会社（SPV）は、アルファベット傘下のグーグルとブロードコムが共同開発したカスタム半導体を購入し、アンソロピックにリースする。リース料を裏付けとしてSPVが発行する資産担保証券（ABS）は、私募証券市場の144a市場で取引される。

インパックス・アセットマネジメントの投資適格ポートフォリオマネジャー、トニー・トシチンカ氏は「ブロードコムのCDSスプレッド上昇は、AI投資への全般的な不安というより同社のバランスシートに起因するという印象がある」と指摘した。半導体チップの資金調達ディールでブロードコムが追加的な金融保証を提供する観測に関係している可能性が高いという。

テック企業がクラウドコンピューティング能力の拡充に数十億ドルを投じる中で、今年に入り保証や他の金融支援の利用頻度が増している。ブロードコムやエヌビディアといった半導体チップメーカーは事実上、自社のバランスシートの強みを顧客に提供し、購買力を支えている。

item.title: Tornado in southwestern France damages over 300 homes, injures dozens
item.description: A tornado swept through the Aude region of southwestern France late on Monday, damaging more than 300 homes and injuring dozens, authorities said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A tornado swept through the Aude region of southwestern France late on Monday, damaging more than 300 homes and injuring dozens, authorities said. Thirty-nine people were injured, including two in critical condition in the village of Pomas, local authorities said. By Tuesday morning some 21,000 households were without power in southern France, including 1,600 in the Aude, local grid operator ENEDIS said. "A tornado of rare intensity struck the Aude region late yesterday afternoon, severely damaging the village of Pomas," Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said on X. Social media footage verified by Reuters showed the tornado swirling above the nearby village of Verzeille in Aude, late on Monday. Many of the homes caught up in its path had their windows smashed. The tornado struck as this summer's intense [USN:L8N43V0G8 TEXT:"heatwave"] gave way this week to thunderstorms in many areas of southern France.

item.title: 米がイランの貿易相手に制裁警告 対象となり得る国は
item.description:
米トランプ政権は24日、「経済版Dデー」と銘打ち、イランの主要な貿易相手国を標的とした制裁を科すと表明した。イランの貿易相手とは、どの国か。
＜中国＞
中国はイラン産原油の最大の買い手で、2025年の購入量は日量約138万バレルと推定される。
米財務省は4月、イラン産原油を数十億ドル規模で購入したとして、中国の独立系製油所に制裁を科した。また、中国の銀行に対しても、イラン産原油の取引を仲介した場合には二次制裁の対象となり得ると警告した。
しかし中国政府は過去10年間、米制裁の影響を遮断する製油所システムを構築してきた。これらの製油所は主にイラン産原油を処理しており、米国との取引はほとんどない。
また中国は「違法な一方的制裁に断固反対する」との立場を示している。
＜UAE（アラブ首長国連邦）＞
UAEは長年、イラン経済の生命線の一つであり、今回の紛争前はイランにとって最大級の貿易相手国だった。
世界貿易機関（WTO
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米トランプ政権は24日、「経済版Dデー」と銘打ち、イランの主要な貿易相手国を標的とした制裁を科すと表明した。イランの貿易相手とは、どの国か。

＜中国＞

中国はイラン産原油の最大の買い手で、2025年の購入量は日量約138万バレルと推定される。

米財務省は4月、イラン産原油を数十億ドル規模で購入したとして、中国の独立系製油所に制裁を科した。また、中国の銀行に対しても、イラン産原油の取引を仲介した場合には二次制裁の対象となり得ると警告した。

しかし中国政府は過去10年間、米制裁の影響を遮断する製油所システムを構築してきた。これらの製油所は主にイラン産原油を処理しており、米国との取引はほとんどない。

また中国は「違法な一方的制裁に断固反対する」との立場を示している。

＜UAE（アラブ首長国連邦）＞

UAEは長年、イラン経済の生命線の一つであり、今回の紛争前はイランにとって最大級の貿易相手国だった。

世界貿易機関（WTO）の最新統計によると2024年、UAEからの輸入は210億ドルで、イランの総輸入額のおよそ3割を占めた。また輸出先としてもUAEは13％を占めていた。

だがUAEは最近、イランのミサイル攻撃を理由に、イランとの金融・経済取引を当面の間停止すると発表した。

＜その他の国々＞

ガス供給の13％をイランに依存するトルコは、イランとの重要な経済関係を変更する意向を示していない。

イラクは、年間およそ40─50億ドル相当の天然ガスをイランから輸入している。イラクのエネルギー当局者2人は、米国の新たな制裁が発動されれば、イラン産エネルギー購入を維持する上で大きな課題になり得ると述べた。

インドとイランの貿易額はかつて170億ドルに達した。しかし米国がイラン制裁を強化した2020年に3分の2以上減少し、その後さらに減少している。

item.title: RBI's Mixed Messages
item.description: Two recent moves from the Indian central bank have left investors scratching their heads over which signals matter and which do not. Does the Reserve Bank of India need to rethink the ways it communicates? That's our focus this week. Write to me with your views at ira.dugal@thomsonreuters.com.
item.dc:creator: Ira Dugal
item.content:encoded: (Sign up here to get latest news from India and how it matters to the world) Two recent moves from the Indian central bank have left investors scratching their heads over which signals matter and which do not. Does the Reserve Bank of India need to rethink the ways it communicates? That's our focus this week. Write to me with your views at ira.dugal@thomsonreuters.com . And, a crackdown on food quality in the Indian financial capital Mumbai engulfs large foreign and local brands. Scroll down for more on that. THIS WEEK IN ASIA [USN:L6N44L0PO TEXT:"What are Iran's options to escalate further in face of US economic threats?"] [USN:L6N44L04P TEXT:"Shein fashions bizarre upside-down IPO"] [USN:L1N44L0YQ TEXT:"Japan eyes tax breaks for non-core business sales in governance reform push, sources say"] [USN:L1N44I06K TEXT:"China tax crackdown forces wealthy investors to assess their offshore trusts"] [USN:L1N44L07B TEXT:"Trump's Kim gambit deepens doubts over US reliability at a key moment for Asia"] WORDS VS. ACTIONS "If I seem unduly clear to you, you probably misunderstood what I said." Alan Greenspan's famous quip about central bank communication might be getting a fresh outing in India. The Reserve Bank of India has found itself under fire at least twice in recent weeks over its messaging. The first episode involved a dollar deposit scheme introduced in June to attract foreign currency inflows and support a rupee that had slipped to record lows. The RBI [USN:L4N44B0SX TEXT:"shut the scheme"] a month early, just a week after Governor Sanjay Malhotra was asked about a potential early closure and said no such proposal was on the table "as of now". Because the RBI never specified how much money it hoped to attract or how it viewed the costs attached to it, markets assumed the scheme would run its full course. The [USN:L1N44E03Q TEXT:"surprise closure"], probably a result of [USN:L6N43Q0HZ TEXT:"stronger-than-expected inflows"], nevertheless rattled currency and bond markets. While the RBI could not have stated an explicit target, "it would have helped if the RBI were more explicit about costs and attendant liquidity and repayment implications to balance expectations," said Dhiraj Nim, economist and FX strategist at ANZ Research. Days later, investors were wrong-footed again when [USN:L4N44G13Q TEXT:"minutes"] from the RBI's August rate-setting meeting struck a notably less dovish tone than the [USN:L1N442056 TEXT:"policy itself"]. The meeting had been read to suggest the panel was in no hurry to raise rates. Policymakers said inflation pressures were largely supply-driven and showed "little" sign of broadening, prompting analysts to [USN:L4N4430BH TEXT:"rein in"] rate-hike expectations. Yet the minutes suggested policymakers were already contemplating tighter policy. The rise in average headline and core inflation "may suggest a recalibration of policy rate," Malhotra said in the minutes, in a far clearer signal of tighter monetary policy than was offered at the time of the rate decision. "There is a clear disconnect," State Bank of India chief economist Soumya Kanti Ghosh wrote, pointing to both the deposit-window surprise and differences between the policy statement, the press conference following the decision and meeting minutes. The RBI did not reply to Reuters' emailed request for comment. COMMUNICATING THROUGH UNCERTAINTY To be fair, the RBI is hardly alone. Ghosh described central banks globally as navigating a "communication quagmire" in an unusually uncertain environment. The U.S. Federal Reserve's new chairman Kevin Warsh has largely shunned forward guidance and opted not to participate in the "dot plot" that investors use to gauge future interest rates. The retreat from guidance has [USN:L6N43Q12Z TEXT:"vexed markets"] and may be an "own goal," Breakingviews columnist Felix Martin recently argued. [USN:L6N43Q0HZ TEXT:"Read here."] Sign up for Reuters Econ World newsletter here . Hints of a similar philosophy surfaced in comments from RBI Executive Director Indranil Bhattacharyya in the August meeting minutes. Rather than offering "forward guidance", he said, the central bank is providing "framework guidance". Understanding the RBI's inflation framework and policy "reaction function", he argued, offers a better clue to future decisions. The challenge is that India's framework leaves room for interpretation. While the RBI targets 4% inflation, it is allowed a tolerance band of 2% to 6% to accommodate food and fuel shocks given the dominance of these items in India's inflation basket. Markets therefore struggle to judge whether policymakers would react only when inflation threatens the upper end of that band in times of supply shocks, or much earlier. For now, Bhattacharyya's comments may offer the clearest clue. Noting that 69% of inflation-weighted items are currently rising by less than 4%, he argued that policymakers "must look out for the extent of generalisation and risk of inflation expectations getting unanchored before contemplating any rate hike". FOOD QUALITY CRACKDOWN The food safety chief of the western Indian state of Maharashtra has [USN:L1N44C01A TEXT:"intensified a crackdown"] on the food industry over poor hygiene. A number of well-known local eateries have been asked to stop operations and permits of a dozen warehouses of Indian grocery giants Eternal, Swiggy and Zepto have been suspended after inspectors found cockroaches crawling over rusted and dirty food storage racks. Read here for more on the maverick food safety chief [USN:L4N44I0DL TEXT:"Tukaram Mundhe"]. The national food safety regulator is also investigating the alcohol industry, inspecting a Pernod Ricard factory and pushing for better hygiene, Reuters' Aditya Kalra reported. [USN:L4N44G1BO TEXT:"Read here for more"]. The regulator also [USN:L6N43Z05B TEXT:"banned"] several whisky and rum brands made by the Indian unit of Diageo and Inbrew Beverages after discovering the companies had been adding flavourings to achieve the drinks' distinctive aroma and taste rather than the age-old natural process. Diageo later said it would [USN:L4N44E10L TEXT:"reformulate"] some of its popular brands. MARKET MATTERS Russia's share of India's oil imports has surged to a record high, driven by disruptions to Middle East supply triggered by the Iran war. India's Russian crude buying faces uncertainty after legislation passed by the U.S. Senate this month to impose tariffs of 100% on buyers of Russian oil, Reuters' Nidhi Verma reports. [USN:L4N4490ZW TEXT:"Read here"]. Russian Urals crude delivered to India has [USN:L6N44I0RI TEXT:"flipped to a premium"] because of the strong demand.

item.title: Russia's Afipsky oil refinery on fire after drone attack, two dead, governor says
item.description: The Afipsky oil refinery in Russia's southern Krasnodar region was on fire following a drone attack, regional Governor Veniamin Kondratyev said on the Telegram messaging app on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Afipsky oil refinery in Russia's southern Krasnodar region was on fire following a drone attack, regional Governor Veniamin Kondratyev said on the Telegram messaging app on Tuesday. He added that two people were killed and two others were injured due to falling drone debris on the Afipsky railway station. Ukraine has been targeting Russia's oil refineries and other infrastructure, attempting to undermine Moscow's war efforts and reduce financial revenue. In a recent case, the Perm oil refinery, Russia's seventh-largest oil processing plant by volume, [USN:L1N44L0IX TEXT:"stopped operations"] following a Ukrainian drone attack, which caused fire and damage to its technological units on August 21, according to two industry sources. The Afipsky plant is mostly export-focused. It processed 7.2 million metric tons of crude oil (144,000 barrels per day) in 2024. It has been [USN:L6N4480EU TEXT:"targeted by Ukrainian drones"] several times in the past number of months.

item.title: German investigators find third drone, explosives after failed airport attack, media say
item.description: German investigators discovered a third drone and suspected explosives linked to this month's attempted attack on the Leipzig/Halle airport, broadcasters NDR and WDR and the Sueddeutsche Zeitung newspaper said on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: German investigators discovered a third drone and suspected explosives linked to this month's attempted attack on the Leipzig/Halle airport, broadcasters NDR and WDR and the Sueddeutsche Zeitung newspaper said on Tuesday. The drone was found on August 14, 10 days after the [USN:L8N4420IV TEXT:"incident"], to the west of the airport, where investigators also discovered about 50 grams (1.8 oz) of a substance they suspected to be the military explosive hexogen, the media reports said. The office of the prosecutor general did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. Security sources cited in the reports suspect Russian intelligence involvement in the attempted attack, an accusation Moscow has denied. On August 4, an explosives-laden drone was discovered near a Ukrainian Antonov cargo aircraft used for military supplies. Investigators also suspect a second drone may have collided with a DHL cargo plane soon after the airport's temporary shutdown. The airport is a cargo and military logistics hub used by NATO and Ukraine's Antonov Airlines for military supplies.

item.title: Gold Fields posts 81% jump in half-year profit, boosts dividend
item.description: South Africa's Gold Fields said on Tuesday its half-year profit rose 81%, driven by higher gold prices, output and sales.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: South Africa's Gold Fields (GFIJ.J) said on Tuesday its half-year profit rose 81%, driven by higher gold prices, output and sales. The Johannesburg-based miner reported headline earnings per share of $2.08 for the six months to June 30, up from $1.15 a year earlier. Gold Fields said it would pay a dividend of 16.25 rand ($1.01) per share, an increase of 133% on last year's interim payout. Gold prices have been supported by safe-haven buying and expectations of U.S. interest rate cuts. Gains were capped, however, by a stronger dollar and concerns that higher oil prices linked to the Middle East conflict could fuel inflation. Gold Fields' gold output was 12% higher at 1.267 million ounces during the first half of 2026, compared with the prior period. It maintained its full-year gold production guidance of 2.4 to 2.6 million ounces. ($1 = 16.0186 rand)

item.title: Bitcoin rises above $80,000 as soft dollar, debasement fears boost momentum
item.description: Bitcoin rose above $80,000 to hit a more than three-month high on Tuesday as a soft U.S. dollar, in the wake of the moves by Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent to calm the bond market, revived momentum in the crypto sector.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Bitcoin rose above $80,000 to hit a more than three-month high on Tuesday as a soft U.S. dollar, in the wake of the moves by Treasury Secretary [USN:L1N44L0RK TEXT:"Scott Bessent"] to calm the bond market, revived momentum in the crypto sector. U.S. President Donald Trump last week [USN:L1N44G0GU TEXT:"called"] on Congress to pass a bill that would bring clearer definitions to the growing cryptocurrency sector. Since then, bitcoin , the world's largest cryptocurrency, has risen 16%. It was last at $80,323.24 in Asian hours, having earlier touched $81,237.94, its highest level since mid-May. Bitcoin is up 28% so far in August, set for its biggest monthly gain since November 2024. Cryptocurrencies also got a big boost after the U.S. Treasury last week [USN:L1N44G0GD TEXT:"unveiled plans"] to buy back more long-dated bonds to help cap the gains in the long-end yields, a move that has led to the U.S. dollar bearing the brunt of investor angst. Tim Sun, senior researcher at HashKey Group, said Bessent's messaging has reinforced the market's view that, at least through the midterm elections, U.S. policymakers may have a lower tolerance for a further rise in long-end yields. "That would create a relatively supportive macro backdrop for assets such as bitcoin and gold," Sun said. Gold has been the other beneficiary of the dollar weakness, rising to a three-month high. The Treasury announcement is "exactly the type of thing bitcoin loves," Geoff Kendrick, global head of digital assets research at Standard Chartered, said in a note last week, adding that bitcoin was built to allow investors a way to avoid this type of intervention. The action stoked increased chatter around the so-called [USN:L1N44H0RB TEXT:"debasement trade"], where the moves to prevent long-end yields from reaching market-clearing levels via buybacks lead the pressure to shift from the bond market to the currency market. "This (Treasury announcement) prompted buyers to scramble into physical and digital assets as debasement trade fears re-emerged," said Tony Sycamore, market analyst at IG. "A sustained break above here would open the door for a move towards $95,000–$100,000."

item.title: Angel Reese grabs WNBA-record 26 rebounds in Dream's win over Sparks
item.description: Angel Reese grabbed a WNBA-record 26 rebounds, Allisha Gray scored 20 points and the Atlanta Dream completed a perfect West Coast road trip with a 78-71 victory over the Los Angeles Sparks on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Angel Reese grabbed a WNBA-record 26 rebounds, Allisha Gray scored 20 points and the Atlanta Dream completed a perfect West Coast road trip with a 78-71 victory over the Los Angeles Sparks on Monday. Rhyne Howard scored 18 points and Naz Hillmon had 12 for the Dream (25-13), who went 4-0 on their trip and moved within a half game of third place in the overall standings with six regular-season games remaining. Reese broke Chamique Holdsclaw's record of 24 rebounds set in 2003 and added 11 points for her 27th double-double of the season as Atlanta won at Los Angeles for the second time in five days. Earlier in the game, she broke the WNBA single-season rebound mark with her 452nd board of the campaign. She finished the game with 458 rebounds on the season. Las Vegas' A'ja Wilson set the previous mark in 2024. Nneka Ogwumike scored a season-high 27 points with 16 rebounds and Cameron Brink had 15 points with five blocks off the bench as the Sparks (13-25) lost for the seventh time in eight games. Los Angeles was eliminated from playoff contention with a loss to Atlanta on Thursday. Dearica Hamby also had 15 points for the Sparks, who were without guard and third-leading scorer Rae Burrell (illness). Los Angeles picked up its defensive intensity in its second game against Atlanta during a four-game homestand. The Dream scored a franchise-high 124 points against the Sparks last week but were nowhere near that total Monday while shooting 40.0% from the floor. The Dream led 20-15 after one quarter before going up by as many as six points in the second quarter and taking a 37-36 lead into halftime. Ogwumike lead all scorers in the first half with 12 points. Atlanta took control in the third quarter behind nine points from Gray and took a 62-55 lead into the final period. The Dream took their first double-digit lead at 66-55 with 9:05 remaining and were never threatened over the final 10 minutes. The victory gave Atlanta a perfect 3-0 record against Los Angeles this season. --Field Level Media

item.title: Zara clothing supplier Pearl Global evaluates Africa expansion as Europe demand grows
item.description: India's Pearl Global is exploring manufacturing opportunities in North Africa and countries like Jordan as the Zara clothing supplier looks to move production closer to European customers and diversify beyond the United States, a top executive said.
item.dc:creator: Praveen Paramasivam
item.content:encoded: India's Pearl Global (PGIL.NS) is exploring manufacturing opportunities in North Africa and countries like Jordan as the Zara clothing supplier looks to move production closer to European customers and diversify beyond the United States, a top executive said. The potential move reflects a broader recalibration by Indian garment manufacturers, which are looking to tap growing European demand amid shifts in U.S. trade policy and disruptions to global shipping routes linked to Middle East tensions. "We are again evaluating things," Managing Director Pallab Banerjee told Reuters, adding that Pearl, which also supplies Levi's and Gap apparel, could pursue partnerships closer to Europe. The clothing manufacturer, which also has operations in Bangladesh, Vietnam, Indonesia and Guatemala, counts the U.S. as its largest market but the country's share of Pearl's revenue has steadily reduced to about 50% currently from more than 85% in fiscal 2021 as it expands in Spain, Britain, Japan and Australia. The European Union accounted for 16% to 17% of group revenue in fiscal 2026. Rival Raymond Lifestyle (RAYL.NS) , which counts Ted Baker and Charles Tyrwhitt among its customers, is [USN:L4N4432BR TEXT:"increasing production"] at its Ethiopia facility as European orders grow. Gokaldas Exports (GOKL.NS) , which manufactures in Kenya and Ethiopia besides India, also expects to ramp up its existing capacity in the continent later this year as Indian apparel exporters seek to lower their dependence on the U.S. market. Pearl set up operations in Guatemala, in Central America, after the COVID pandemic to better supply its U.S. clients, Banerjee said. The company also expects revenue growth of more than 15% in fiscal 2027 after reporting a 12% rise in the previous year. Banerjee also said the company could achieve its fiscal 2028 revenue target of 60 billion rupees ($626.75 million) ahead of schedule. Its revenue stood at 50.25 billion rupees in the year to March 31. ($1 = 95.7325 Indian rupees)

item.title: Australia court finds dating site eHarmony misled users over subscription terms
item.description: Australia's Federal Court has found online dating platform eHarmony engaged in misleading or deceptive conduct by misrepresenting aspects of its subscription services, the country's consumer watchdog said on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Australia's Federal Court has found online dating platform eHarmony engaged in misleading or deceptive conduct by misrepresenting aspects of its subscription services, the country's consumer watchdog said on Tuesday. The ruling followed proceedings brought by the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) in September 2023, which alleged the company breached the Australian Consumer Law through statements made on its website and mobile application. The regulator said that the court found the U.S.-based firm had breached Consumer Law by engaging in misleading or deceptive conduct relating to free access, automatic renewals, membership length, cancellation rights and pricing disclosures. The court found that eHarmony did not prominently disclose the automatic renewal terms, and instead presented them in small font late in the purchasing process and within terms and conditions. The court also found that the company breached Consumer Law by advertising monthly prices without clearly displaying the minimum total amount consumers would pay over the full subscription term, the ACCC added. "The ACCC is concerned about subscription traps in digital services, and this decision highlights the need for clarity in ongoing consumer subscriptions," ACCC Commissioner Luke Woodward said. The court will determine penalties, consumer redress and other orders sought by the ACCC at a later date. In an emailed response to Reuters, eHarmony said that it was "carefully reviewing the Federal Court’s judgment" and considering its options.

item.title: RBA says reserves still above demand amid shift to new liquidity system
item.description: Australia's central bank said on Tuesday reserves in the financial system were still above underlying demand as it shifts to a new system that will provide enough liquidity to banks while keeping rates anchored near the official cash rate.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Australia's central bank said on Tuesday reserves in the financial system were still above underlying demand as it shifts to a new system that will provide enough liquidity to banks while keeping rates anchored near the official cash rate. In a speech on the ample reserves policy, Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) Head of Domestic Markets David Jacobs said reserves have fallen by more than half since 2022 as the assets the central bank acquired under pandemic-era policies have matured, and that will continue. However, funds can still be sourced cheaply in short-term repo markets and the use of the full-allotment open market operations under the new system is still modest, he added. "Taken together, those indicators suggest that we're not yet in an environment where the level of reserves is driven by demand," said Jacobs. "When we might reach ample reserves ultimately remains highly uncertain. It could be some years away... But it could also be earlier if banks increase their demand or there are market frictions." The RBA said in 2024 that it would shift to a system of ample reserves to set interest rates, in which banks' demands for reserves are satisfied via open market repo operations at a price near the cash rate target. That ended the old system of setting a floor for rates with excess reserves and an exchange settlement (ES) rate.

item.title: Six months into Iran war, almost half of global oil flows from war zones
item.description: Almost half the world's oil comes from countries affected by conflict in 2026, Reuters calculations show, underscoring that current disruptions have eclipsed previous energy crises.
item.dc:creator: Seher Dareen, Anushree Mukherjee, Robert Harvey
item.content:encoded: Almost half the world's oil comes from countries affected by conflict in 2026, Reuters calculations show, underscoring that current disruptions have eclipsed previous energy crises. Six months ago, U.S. and Israeli attacks on Iran triggered what has become the largest oil supply crisis on record, with no clear end [USN:L8N44F0XM TEXT:"in sight"]. At the same time, the Russia-Ukraine war has forced production and refining cuts, including in nearby Kazakhstan this year. Ongoing conflict in Libya and U.S. restrictions on Venezuelan oil exports at the start of the year have added further strain. Together, countries affected by those conflicts produced about 45 million barrels per day of oil based on 2025 output, accounting for more than 43% of global supply, according to Reuters calculations using International Energy Agency data. The disruptions have increased the world's reliance on U.S. oil supplies, though that too has occasionally been disrupted by [USN:L6N3YR146 TEXT:"severe weather"]. Not all of this year's supply disruptions happened at the same time. With Saudi Arabia re-routing oil to the Red Sea and Gulf exporters [USN:L6N42O0JF TEXT:"sneaking oil secretly out"] of the Strait of Hormuz, the current Gulf oil disruption stands at around 5 million to 7 million bpd, according to analysts' estimates. But risks to total flows remain high, as [USN:L1N44E0BO TEXT:"attacks in the Red Sea"] and near [USN:L6N43W0MR TEXT:"Egypt's Suez Canal"] in July demonstrated. The conflicts in the Gulf and [USN:L6N4400MZ TEXT:"Ukraine"] have also cut global refining capacity by about a [USN:L6N41Q19F TEXT:"tenth"]. Ukraine has targeted much of Russia's refining network, striking plants as far away as Omsk, about 2,700 km (1,680 miles) from Ukrainian-held territory. Russia is grappling with fuel shortages and has banned gasoline and diesel exports, tightening global fuel markets. Higher fuel prices have become a key driver of inflation, contributing to higher borrowing costs and helping to push [USN:L6N44G17Z TEXT:"U.S. debt to a record $40 trillion"]. U.S. diesel prices have climbed to [USN:L1N44E0K1 TEXT:"record levels"] despite refiners running at peak capacity. The IEA has released record volumes from emergency stockpiles to help cushion the supply shock. Those releases are now largely complete, even as global inventories continue to [USN:L4N43O0HZ TEXT:"decline"].

item.title: 中国、道交法に自動運転規則を新設へ メーカー・輸入業者に責任も
item.description: [北京 ２５日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[北京 ２５日 ロイター] - 中国当局が道路交通安全法に自動運転車に関する規則を追加する案を提示したと、国営新華社通信が伝えた。

２５日に全国人民代表大会（全人代）常務委員会の審議のため提出された改正案は、自動運転と運転支援の機能を定義し、責任範囲を明確にする内容。

自動運転モードで走行中の交通違反については、メーカーまたは輸入業者が責任を問われる可能性がある。一方、手動運転または運転支援機能のみで走行していた車両については、引き続き現行の交通規則が適用されるという。

item.title: Death of the consumer conglomerate? Unilever bets less is more
item.description: Unilever is betting that shedding food assets and focusing on beauty, personal care and home products will close a valuation gap with more focused rivals. The challenge is convincing investors that a simpler company can deliver higher returns.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Marrow, Richa Naidu
item.content:encoded: Unilever is betting that shedding food assets and focusing on beauty, personal care and home products will close a valuation gap with more focused rivals. The challenge is convincing investors that a simpler company can deliver higher returns. The maker of Dove soap, Axe deodorant and Cif cleaning products trades at 11.5 times enterprise value to core earnings, according to LSEG data. That compares with 14.8 for Procter & Gamble, 17.5 for L'Oreal and 22.7 for Coca-Cola. Those multiples suggest investors place a premium on more focused consumer goods companies. But investors have two main concerns. Unilever's (ULVR.L) [USN:L6N40J0DU TEXT:"deal in March "]to merge its food business with U.S. spice maker McCormick will leave the British group with an almost 10% stake in the combined company, and its shareholders with a roughly 55% stake. At the same time, the transaction reduces Unilever's exposure to a relatively high-margin business, increasing pressure on management to show that faster-growing beauty, personal care and home products can make up the difference. "Until you show me the evidence that you're turning this around, you're sitting on a very low multiple," said Dan Hanbury, a portfolio manager at Ninety One, a major investor in Colgate-Palmolive, Unilever and L'Oreal. The market is wary of "false dawns" from corporate turnarounds, he added, saying Unilever probably needed three or four quarters of strong volume growth to win over doubters. THE P&G EXAMPLE Big industrial companies from General Electric to Siemens have spent years simplifying their structures in an effort to eliminate what investors call a conglomerate discount, a penalty applied to companies whose complexity is seen as weighing on efficiency and growth. That thinking has increasingly spread to consumer goods companies. Where diversification was once seen as a strength that could cushion changes in consumer tastes, investors now increasingly favour category leaders that can focus investment, innovation and marketing on a narrower set of products. Under CEO Fernando Fernandez, Unilever has accelerated its retreat from food. The company spun off its ice cream business and in March struck a roughly $65 billion deal to combine its food division with McCormick. The issue is not that food is unprofitable. The business has historically generated attractive margins, but growth has lagged Unilever's beauty and personal care operations. "Being focused on a single category allows you to be more cost effective and more innovative," said Akeel Sachak, global head of consumer at Rothschild & Co. Investors often point to Procter & Gamble as a template. The Tide detergent maker exited food and streamlined its brand portfolio, subsequently delivering stronger growth and earning a valuation premium for much of the following decade. "P&G pulled off the restructuring, drove higher growth and commanded a relatively higher premium for probably 10 years," Hanbury said. IMPROVING RESULTS Investors and analysts say the focus for Unilever has now switched from portfolio reshuffling to execution. "If (Unilever) continues to execute, Unilever will continue to see a degree of re-rating ... and then hopefully grow from there," said Will James, portfolio manager at Guinness Global Investors, which holds shares in Unilever and L'Oreal. Unilever has reported improving results in recent quarters, and in July said sales volumes had reached their highest level in more than [USN:L4N43U0F3 TEXT:"a decade"]. Yet despite the operational improvement, some Unilever investors are concerned about their continued exposure to the slow-growing food category via their stake in the company resulting from the McCormick merger, Barclays analyst Warren Ackerman said. Unilever declined to comment. CEO Fernando Fernandez told an industry event in June: "I believe that every quarter that goes by, and we deliver the numbers that we have been delivering, and we get closer to the closing of a transaction of McCormick, the value of Unilever will be shown."

item.title: Nvidia shares set for $280 billion price swing after earnings, options show
item.description: Options traders are pricing in a $280 billion swing in Nvidia's market value after the company reports second-quarter earnings on Wednesday afternoon, as investors seek fresh insight into the demand driving the technology sector.
item.dc:creator: Laura Matthews
item.content:encoded: Options traders are pricing in a $280 billion swing in Nvidia's (NVDA.O) market value after the company reports second-quarter earnings on Wednesday afternoon, as investors seek fresh insight into the demand driving the technology sector. The chipmaker's options are pricing in a 5.4% move in either direction on Thursday, a day after the company reports results, which is [USN:L6N41V13R TEXT:"below the 6.5%"] move implied ahead of its May earnings report. The implied move translates to about $280 billion in market capitalization — more than the individual market value of about 90% of S&P 500 constituents. The expected move also remains well below Nvidia's historical average price swing of 7.4% over the last 12 quarters, according to analytics firm Option Research & Technology Services (ORATS). "That shows some complacency for Nvidia, and it means it's getting more predictable," said Matt Amberson, founder of ORATS. The relatively modest moves reflect a pattern over the past two years in which actual post-earnings stock swings have frequently fallen short of what options markets had priced in, said Chris Murphy, co-head of derivatives strategy at Susquehanna, a market maker. "I think the beginning of the AI era when Nvidia was surprising everybody with the huge earnings beats and 10, 15, 20 percent moves, that's kind of over," said Murphy. "There's just not a huge view that they're going to catch everybody off-guard with some giant beat and the stock's going to really rally." Nvidia shares on Monday posted a decline for the seventh consecutive trading day, but they have risen 11.7% this year. The S&P 500 (.SPX) is up 11.8% year-to-date and the Philadelphia SE Semiconductor index (.SOX) has risen 61%. BROADER MARKET PRESSURES Nvidia's pullback has come at a time of broad market unease. Concerns over rising energy prices and mounting U.S. government debt have pushed Treasury yields higher, with 30-year yields last week hitting a 19-year high and prompting the Treasury [USN:FWN44G0QP TEXT:"to unveil measures"] aimed at easing market strains. Reports that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent could draw on the government's nearly $1 trillion Treasury General Account to help fund bond buybacks rather than increase issuance sent the 30-year yield a tad lower on Monday, though it still hovered above 5%. The recent yield surge has hit growth and technology stocks, pushing Wall Street's major stock indexes lower and heightening focus on Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh's planned speech in Jackson Hole, Wyoming, later this week. It may provide clues on how policymakers view the economic outlook, particularly for interest rates. Against this backdrop, investors will be watching Nvidia's revenue guidance, chip demand, profit margin and whether major cloud providers continue to increase AI-related capital spending. As the dominant supplier of AI chips, Nvidia is viewed as a bellwether for the broader AI trade. Nvidia recently [USN:L4N44719P TEXT:"partnered with six major financial institutions"] on financing platforms targeting more than $500 billion for AI infrastructure, highlighting the massive capital required as companies and governments race to build data centers for AI workloads. Nvidia probably has "a pretty good pulse on the hyperscaler capex trajectory. Return on investment from the hyperscalers is really important," said Will Sterling, chief investment officer at TritonPoint Wealth. "That will dictate whether or not they continue to invest with their capex. If that happens, then I think that'll be beneficial from a risk-on perspective in the entire ecosystem."

item.title: Cal Raleigh hits historic trio of homers in Mariners' win over Phillies
item.description: Cal Raleigh became the first Seattle Mariners player to hit three home runs in a game at T-Mobile Park, giving the hosts a 9-2 victory against the Philadelphia Phillies on Monday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Cal Raleigh became the first Seattle Mariners player to hit three home runs in a game at T-Mobile Park, giving the hosts a 9-2 victory against the Philadelphia Phillies on Monday night. The last Seattle player to hit three homers at home was Hall of Famer Edgar Martinez, who did so May 18, 1999, at the Kingdome. The team moved across the street into its new stadium later that summer. Julio Rodriguez and Cole Young also went deep for the Mariners and right-hander Logan Gilbert (11-7) pitched five solid innings. J.T. Realmuto homered for the Phillies, who had a nine-game winning streak snapped. Rodriguez and Raleigh both homered in a five-run first inning against Phillies right-hander Zack Wheeler (10-5), who dropped his fourth straight decision. The Phillies scored in the first as Kyle Schwarber drew a leadoff walk and Bryce Harper and Luis Arraez singled with one out to load the bases. Schwarber scored on Alec Bohm's groundout to second. In the bottom of the inning, Randy Arozarena drew a leadoff walk, Dominic Canzone grounded a single to right and Rodriguez hit a three-run blast off the back wall of the Phillies' bullpen in left field. Josh Naylor was thrown out trying to stretch a single to right into a double before Taylor Ward walked. Raleigh then launched a towering two-run shot to right. Realmuto hit a liner over the wall with one out in the second to pull the Phillies within 5-2. The Mariners scored in the third as Rodriguez and Naylor singled and Ward walked to load the bases. Rodriguez raced home on a wild pitch. Raleigh and Young hit back-to-back homers to right leading off the fifth to make it 8-2 and end Wheeler's evening. Wheeler allowed eight runs on nine hits, with five walks and four strikeouts in four-plus innings. Raleigh lined a solo shot over the wall in right with one out in the seventh off reliever Chase Shugart. Gilbert gave up two runs on five hits, with two walks and five strikeouts in five innings. Seranthony Dominguez, Gabe Speier and Carlos Vargas combined for four innings of perfect relief. --Field Level Media

item.title: Australian bank investors brace for tough times as mortgage demand plummets
item.description: Investors are questioning the rich valuations on Australia's biggest banks as a downturn in lucrative mortgage lending threatens to stifle growth and intensify competition for borrowers.
item.dc:creator: Christine Chen, Scott Murdoch
item.content:encoded: Investors are questioning the rich valuations on Australia's biggest banks as a downturn in lucrative mortgage lending threatens to stifle growth and intensify competition for borrowers. The so-called "Big Four" banks each reported double-digit falls in home-loan applications, citing recent tax policy [USN:L1N41P0EF TEXT:"changes"] and [USN:P8N43N01C TEXT:"higher interest rates"], in an otherwise strong set of August results. The outlook reinforced investor fears of a tougher trading environment for the sector that has for years delivered reliable dividends and outperformed the broader market. "It does feel like the outlook is deteriorating and there's not a whole lot of bright spots that can be talked about," said Minh Pham, a senior investment analyst at Milford Asset Management. "We're definitely more on the bearish side," she added. Weaker growth prospects for the Big Four banks — ANZ (ANZ.AX) , Commonwealth Bank (CBA.AX) , National Australia Bank (NAB.AX) and Westpac (WBC.AX) — will weigh on the Australian equity market, as they make up about 24% of the benchmark S&P/ASX 200 (.AXJO) index and are among the most heavily owned local stocks by global institutional and domestic investors. Together the four control more than 70% of the country's A$2.5 trillion ($1.77 trillion) mortgage market. That dominance has helped push Australia's banks to be among the most expensive in the world. On a forward price to earnings ratio, they are more expensive than JPMorgan (JPM.N) , Citigroup (C.N) , Bank of America (BAC.N) and HSBC (HSBA.L) . Following their quarterly reports, the Australian banks are trading at a price-to-earnings multiple of between 16.2 to 24 times, compared to the larger foreign rivals which sit at 14 to 15 times. They still hold a premium despite share price declines of between 2% and 12% in three of the four major Australian banks this year, against gains of between 11% and 30% for those four international banks. HOUSING PAIN There is downside risk to 2027 earnings from a slowing mortgage market, rising competition, and weaker credit quality, analysts at Morgan Stanley said, adding this strengthened the case for a de-rating of their shares. Housing demand in Australia has [USN:L4N42H0L6 TEXT:"weakened"] since the government scrapped generous tax concessions to property investors, threatening the major driver of revenue for the banks. Auction clearance rates have fallen to the lowest levels in six years and national average prices are down about 2% over four months, according to data from property consultant Cotality. As a result, home-loan applications have slumped, with [USN:L1N44603T TEXT:"Westpac"] reporting the steepest fall, 20%, in its third-quarter update. [USN:L1N44D060 TEXT:"National Australia Bank"] and [USN:L4N4481J7 TEXT:"Commonwealth Bank"] both said loan applications had dropped 15%, while [USN:L4N4491P0 TEXT:"ANZ"] flagged a 12% decline. Citi has forecast a "substantial" slowdown in revenue growth for the sector to 2.9% in the 2027 financial year from 4.4%. In the latest sign of pain in the property sector, a residential developer, Bathla Group, called in external administrators to restructure [USN:L1N44M01W TEXT:"$3.2 billion in debt"], citing a "perfect storm of circumstances". While Citi said banks with a bigger exposure to business lending would fare better, some investors are questioning how much that can offset the retail segment's headwinds. The "wealth effect" from softer house prices and weaker consumer spending could also impact the business credit growth pipeline, Pham said. Relative to other parts of the Australian equity market, the banks look expensive, said Cameron McCormack, senior portfolio manager at VanEck. "From a valuation standpoint, we think that the banks are probably a little bit too expensive," he said. "We think there's better growth at a reasonable price available particularly among mid caps and small caps at the moment." Softer demand for home loans will only intensify competition among the banks. "It's a tough lending environment," said Mark Nathan, head of fundamental research at Regal Funds Management. "(Loan) volumes will moderate, but also you've got everybody competing for a small pie." ($1 = 1.4142 Australian dollars)

item.title: Tesla raises prices of Cybertrucks in the US
item.description: Tesla raised the prices of some of its Cybertruck pickup trucks in the United States on Tuesday, according to its website.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Tesla (TSLA.O) raised the prices of some of its Cybertruck pickup trucks in the United States on Tuesday, according to its website. The company increased the price of its Cybertruck dual motor and premium all-wheel drive by $5,000 to $74,990 and $84,990 respectively.

item.title: Australia coach Kiss wants Suaalii in Wallabies midfield
item.description: Australia coach Les Kiss has no plans to shift Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii to the outside backs despite the growing competition for places in the Wallabies midfield ahead of the two-test series against Argentina.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Australia coach Les Kiss has no plans to shift Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii to the outside backs despite the growing competition for places in the Wallabies midfield ahead of the two-test series against Argentina. Dual code international Suaalii missed the last test against Japan with a hamstring strain but is expected to be available for the opener in San Salvador on Saturday. In his absence, Isaac Henry performed well in the number 13 jersey in [USN:L6N44E0FG TEXT:"Townsville"] in a midfield pairing with Hunter Paisami, while centre [USN:L6N44K0A9 TEXT:"Len Ikitau's return to fitness"] has also given Kiss options. Suaalii has experience as a test winger and as a fullback for the New South Wales Waratahs in Super Rugby Pacific but Kiss poured cold water on the prospect of redeploying the versatile 23-year-old. "No. The intention from the start has been to keep him at outside centre, and that remains the preferred position for now," he told reporters in San Salvador. "However, the back five need flexibility. Players are being asked what other positions they can productively fill, allowing the team to broaden its selection options and deal with different situations. "Suaalii has already moved to the wing, while the team's No. 10s can also play fullback. That positional flexibility is important, but for the moment the preference is to persist with Suaalii at 13." Since taking over the Wallabies for the Japan series, Kiss has shown a willingness to try new things and had two poachers operating in his back row in the second half in Townsville when Fraser McReight joined Carlo Tizzano on the field. The ploy proved effective and revived memories of Michael Cheika's "Pooper" combination of David Pocock and Michael Hooper which helped Australia reach the 2015 World Cup final. Kiss said it was "certainly enticing" to put McReight and Tizzano to work again but did not see it as a fixture going forward. "There are also other combinations involving the team's power in the back row that the coaches want to explore," he said. Kiss praised his players for buying into new mechanisms and ideas brought by the new Wallabies staff, and said their work on defence under Scott McLeod, a former All Blacks assistant coach at the last two World Cups, had already paid dividends. The tests against Argentina would be a good measure of their progress, he added, as the Wallabies build toward next year's home World Cup. "Once the (Argentina) crowd gets going, it can become a very difficult environment, so Australia will need to be good enough to quell that and withstand it," he said.

item.title: Fortescue suspends senior executive under sexual harassment probe
item.description: Fortescue , Australia's third-largest miner, said on Tuesday it had suspended a senior executive who is under investigation over allegations of sexual harassment and bullying.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Fortescue (FMG.AX) , Australia's third-largest miner, said on Tuesday it had suspended a senior executive who is under investigation over allegations of sexual harassment and bullying. Fortescue was taking the allegations "[USN:L8N44G266 TEXT:"extremely seriously"]" and hired law firm MinterEllison to investigate, it said in a statement to Reuters last week. The allegations against the unnamed senior executive were first reported by the Australian Financial Review earlier this month. "As the investigation has progressed, Fortescue has continued to take external legal and governance advice," the miner said on Tuesday. "It has been decided that the employee who is the subject of the allegations will not undertake any work for Fortescue while the investigation continues." The statement came after Fortescue's energy chief, Gus Pichot, told an earnings call last week that legal advice indicated the person did not need to be suspended. "We have taken extensive external legal and governance advice so we are quite confident we are following the proper process," he said. Sexual harassment has been a persistent issue at mine sites in Western Australia and sparked a state inquiry in 2021. Fortescue was served with a class action in July alleging workplace misconduct, including sexual harassment and sex discrimination. The suit was filed by law firm JGA Saddler, which also launched similar class-action lawsuits against Rio Tinto (RIO.AX) and BHP (BHP.AX) in late 2024. Those cases are still winding their way through the courts. Fortescue last week reported a 20% drop in "psychosocial" breaches, which include sexual harassment, ethics issues and other incidents, with 98 incidents reported in the latest financial year. The company, which has 16,154 employees, said it had dismissed 11 people for breaches of its code of conduct relating to discrimination and sexual harassment during the year. It found 13 cases of inappropriate sexual contact, 10 of sexual harassment and one of sexual assault.

item.title: Kerr and Ingebrigtsen to renew 1,500 rivalry next month
item.description: Tokyo Olympics champion Jakob Ingebrigtsen will renew his fierce 1,500m rivalry with Briton Josh Kerr at World Athletics' inaugural Ultimate Championship next month after both athletes received exceptional invitations for the meet.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Tokyo Olympics champion Jakob Ingebrigtsen will renew his fierce 1,500m rivalry with Briton Josh Kerr at World Athletics' inaugural Ultimate Championship next month after both athletes received exceptional invitations for the meet. The pair have met multiple times over 1,500m, with Norway's Ingebrigtsen holding a significant head-to-head advantage over Kerr, though they have not faced each other over the distance since the Zurich Diamond League meeting in 2024. Kerr took bronze behind his rival in Tokyo but beat the Norwegian to win gold at the 2023 world championships. The Scot also took silver behind Cole Hocker at the Paris Olympics two years ago, while Ingebrigtsen finished fourth. The pair have traded barbs over the years, with Ingebrigtsen once referring to Kerr as "just the next guy" and boasting he could beat him blindfolded, while Kerr has said the Norwegian has major weaknesses. Ingebrigtsen stoked the rivalry earlier this month when he said he was [USN:L4N44B04J TEXT:"disappointed not to see Kerr"] at the European Championships and that the sport was being ruined by athletes skipping major competitions. Kerr broke the [USN:L4N43K01Y TEXT:"mile world record"] in July at the London Diamond League and followed that up with a [USN:L4N43Z00F TEXT:"gold medal at the Commonwealth Games"] in front of home fans in Glasgow, before skipping the European Championships to manage his workload. "I've made some choices this season that have created plenty of noise, but I've always wanted to prove myself in the biggest races, against the best in the world," Kerr said in a statement on Monday. The stacked 1,500m field at the September 11 to 13 meet in Budapest also includes American Hocker and Portugal's world champion Isaac Nader.

item.title: Kevin Gausman fires 7 sharp innings as Cubs shut out Diamondbacks
item.description: Michael Conforto and Carson Kelly hit back-to-back homers in a three-run sixth, Kevin Gausman threw seven scoreless innings, and the Chicago Cubs beat the Arizona Diamondbacks 7-0 in Phoenix on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Michael Conforto and Carson Kelly hit back-to-back homers in a three-run sixth, Kevin Gausman threw seven scoreless innings, and the Chicago Cubs beat the Arizona Diamondbacks 7-0 in Phoenix on Monday. Conforto, who also doubled and singled, has homered in two straight games and in three of his past eight. The Cubs have 12 homers in the past four games. Gausman (7-11) gave up three hits, all singles, and one walk while striking out six in his fourth start since joining the Cubs at the trade deadline. The D-backs got only one runner past first base off Gausman, when Corbin Carroll walked with one out in the fourth and stole second and third with two outs. Geraldo Perdomo grounded out to end the inning. Ryan Zeferjahn and Caleb Thielbar each threw a scoreless inning to complete Chicago's sixth shutout win of the season. Ian Happ and rookie Pedro Ramirez each had two hits and an RBI for the Cubs, who have won two straight after a three-game losing streak. The Cubs have scored 26 consecutive runs over two games after giving up the first two runs in a 19-2 victory at Seattle on Sunday. Arizona starter Merrill Kelly (8-12) allowed three runs and five hits with four strikeouts and three walks in 5 2/3 innings. He was removed in a 2-0 game after Ramirez's two-out single in the sixth, and Conforto blasted a 431-foot homer to right on reliever Taylor Clarke's second pitch to push the lead to 4-0. Carson Kelly followed with a 392-foot shot to left. The Cubs added two in the seventh. With one out, Michael Busch walked and Alex Bregman singled before Happ hit an RBI double and Nico Hoerner added a sacrifice fly. The D-backs, who had won three of four, managed only five hits, all singles, and were shut out for the ninth time. They are 3-4 without injured second baseman Ketel Marte. Happ singled and scored on Ramirez's triple to open the scoring in the second, and Conforto came home on Seiya Suzuki's double in the fifth to make it 2-0. The Cubs have won all four games against Arizona this season. --Field Level Media

item.title: Morning Bid: Waiting on Nvidia for next leg of AI rally
item.description: A look at the day ahead in European and global markets from Rae Wee
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A look at the day ahead in European and global markets from Rae Wee It's been a [USN:L1N44M00R TEXT:"muted start to the session"] in Asia on Tuesday, with stocks drifting ahead of Nvidia's earnings this week, where expectations are running sky high for the artificial intelligence darling to deliver stellar results. Technology shares remained under pressure following Alibaba's (9988.HK) launch of a [USN:L6N44L021 TEXT:"$10.2 billion share sale"] at a steep discount to fund its AI ambitions as well as disappointment over Samsung Electronics' (005930.KS) [USN:L1N44L00M TEXT:"shareholder-return plan"] in the previous session. Meanwhile, a roughly 45% slump in the [USN:L4N44K01K TEXT:"shares of Unitree"] since a more than fivefold jump on its Shanghai debut has triggered concerns about bubble risk, retail investor losses and flaws in the IPO system. Shares of China's best-known humanoid robot maker were largely flat on Tuesday, following days of declines since its listing. Much now rides on Nvidia to drive the next leg of the AI rally, given its role as a bellwether for the broader AI ecosystem spanning chipmakers and companies financing the rapid expansion of data center capacity. Elsewhere, oil prices were [USN:L4N44L1KV TEXT:"nursing losses"] after threats from the U.S. for an "economic D-Day" of sanctions on Iran turned out to be a damp squib. The U.S. on Monday unveiled an [USN:L6N44K07T TEXT:"expansion of sanctions"] that it said would cut off Iran's economic lifeline but stopped short of the most punishing measures, instead putting the world on notice to cease doing business with the Islamic Republic. Tehran [USN:L6N44M029 TEXT:"promised to retaliate"] against the sanctions and expressed confidence that major trading partners would resist Washington's pressure campaign. As the war in the Middle East drags on, investors await a string of data releases from Europe this week, including German GDP data and the German Ifo survey later on Tuesday, which could shed light on the economic cost of higher-for-longer energy prices. Key developments that could influence markets on Tuesday: - Germany GDP, Ifo survey - Reopening of 2-year German government debt auction - Reopening of 7-year UK government debt auction - U.S. Conference Board's consumer confidence - Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond President Thomas Barkin speaks

item.title: Rafael Devers' 3-run homer powers Giants past Reds
item.description: Rafael Devers blasted a three-run home run and five relievers took over after injured starter Carson Whisenhunt exited, completing a five-hitter as the San Francisco Giants opened a week-long homestand with a 5-0 victory over the Cincinnati Reds on Monday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Rafael Devers blasted a three-run home run and five relievers took over after injured starter Carson Whisenhunt exited, completing a five-hitter as the San Francisco Giants opened a week-long homestand with a 5-0 victory over the Cincinnati Reds on Monday night. Drew Gilbert doubled twice and scored a pair of runs for the Giants, who teed off on Reds ace Chase Burns (14-3) for all five of their runs in the first two innings en route to snapping a four-game losing streak. Whisenhunt stood to benefit from the early offense until experiencing pain in his left forearm while retiring Sal Stewart for the second out of the third inning. After a visit from the trainer at the mound, the left-hander was pulled from the game, having allowed two hits in his 2 2/3 innings. Jason Foley (1-1) recorded the last out of the third, then teamed with fellow relievers Reiver Sanmartin, Ryan Walker, Carson Seymour and Dylan Smith on 6 1/3 innings of three-hit relief. En route to their 10th shutout of the season, the Giants recorded 11 strikeouts in the game, including three by Whisenhunt. The Giants wasted no time getting to Burns, with Gilbert launching his fifth pitch for a ground-rule double and Devers following two pitches later with a single. Jung Hoo Lee drove in the first run with a single, after which Turner Hill plated Devers with a double. Burns retired the first two Giants he faced in the second before Christian Koss singled and Gilbert doubled again, setting the table for Devers, who crushed his 27th home run for a 5-0 lead. Burns was pulled after 3 2/3 innings, having allowed a season-high-tying five runs and a season-high-tying nine hits. He walked one and struck out five. Reds relievers Sam Moll, Julian Garcia and Emilio Pagan combined for 4 1/3 innings of shutout relief. Koss joined Gilbert and Devers with two hits each for the Giants, who lost an earlier series at Cincinnati 2-1. Tyler Stephenson collected two of the Reds' five hits as Cincinnati lost for the third time in four outings on a nine-game trip. The Reds did not record an extra-base hit on a night when they were out-hit 10-5. --Field Level Media

item.title: Austin Hedges, Parker Messick steer streaking Guardians past Angels
item.description: Austin Hedges slammed a two-run homer for the Cleveland Guardians in a 4-2 victory against the Los Angeles Angels on Monday in Anaheim, Calif.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Austin Hedges slammed a two-run homer for the Cleveland Guardians in a 4-2 victory against the Los Angeles Angels on Monday in Anaheim, Calif. Steven Kwan had two hits and scored a run in the opener of the three-game series for the Guardians, who have won five in a row. Cleveland left-hander Parker Messick (10-8) went six innings, allowing one run and three hits while striking out four and walking one. Angels starter George Klassen (2-2) allowed three runs (two earned) and six hits in 5 1/3 innings during his sixth major league start. The rookie right-hander struck out three and walked three. Josh Lowe had two hits for the Angels, who have lost three of four. Cleveland jumped on top in the third inning. Jose Siri made a diving catch in right field to save extra bases on a leadoff drive by Brayan Rocchio, but Kwan and Jose Ramirez followed with line-drive singles. A walk to Jo Adell loaded the bases before Nathaniel Lowe hit a sacrifice fly to deep center, scoring Kwan and ending Klassen's shutout streak at 12 innings. Messick retired the first nine batters in order before Zach Neto lined a single up the middle to start the fourth. Mike Trout then reached out and lined a two-strike pitch up the middle. Neto took third on the play and Trout took second on the throw to third. One out later, Moises Ballesteros dropped a two-strike single into center field, tying the game 1-1. Angels third baseman Denzer Guzman made a two-base error to start the fifth. Klassen nearly got out of the jam, but Adell came up with two outs and grounded a single up the middle to score Rocchio for a 2-1 lead. Klassen came back out for the sixth and gave up a leadoff walk before exiting after retiring the next batter. Blake Weiman got the second out, but Hedges slammed a two-run homer to left-center to extend the lead to 4-1. The Angels put runners on the corners with one out in the ninth off Guardians closer Cade Smith, and Gustavo Campero delivered a sacrifice fly to cut the gap to 4-2. Smith then induced a flyout from Christian Moore to seal his 34th save. --Field Level Media

item.title: Bank stocks put the lie to an Aussie housing crash
item.description: Rate hikes, tax changes, falling mortgage applications and more are raising fears of the biggest home price drop in 40 years. Yet the Big Four lenders like $188 bln Commonwealth Bank trade on healthy multiples. Unless there's a recession, low housing supply will limit the fall.
item.dc:creator: Antony Currie
item.content:encoded: Fears of a housing crash in Australia are way overblown. That's not to say there aren't risks. Interest rates rising 75 basis points earlier this year was a big blow. But over the past couple of weeks some worrying-looking statistics have spooked the market. But bank stocks indicate worries of a disaster are not built on solid foundations. Applications for mortgages, which account for around 70% of banks' loans and decent chunks of their earnings, fell 20% or more in recent months. Moreover, house prices are down an average 2% or so nationally over roughly the same period, per property research firm Cotality ; they could plummet 15% or more in some cities, reckon analysts at ANZ (ANZ.AX) , which would be the biggest drop since 1983. As a result, shares in the country's Big Four lenders - ANZ, Commonwealth Bank of Australia (CBA.AX) , National Australia Bank (NAB.AX) and Westpac (WBC.AX) - have fallen around 10% on average this month. Yet the lenders all still sport enviable multiples, with Commonwealth's stock at 3.3 times expected book value 12 months from now and its three rivals' between 1.5 and 2 times. That's better than the past two housing downturns in 2017 and 2022, when prices fell around 8%. Why the disconnect? First, the current hit to the banks seems limited to earnings, unlike four years ago when rapidly rising interest rates raised the real prospect of a home loan-sparked credit crunch. Increased commercial lending - not least to the tech, AI and defence sectors - and investment banking are also softening the blow. Crucially, the housing market Down Under has been on a tear this century, with the average dwelling price increasing fivefold, making homes less affordable for many. That was fuelled in part by the right-wing government in 1999 allowing property owners to get tax breaks on investment homes they rented out. The current left-leaning Labor government reversed that in May for new purchases. Unsurprisingly, property investors balked: their mortgage applications plunged 28% at Commonwealth since May, compared with a 9% decline from wannabe owner-occupiers. Imagine that leads to a 10% decline from the national peak in March: that would only put prices back to where they were 15 months earlier. In the frothy Perth market, buyers would only time-travel back to September. There's also a pretty concrete, albeit alarming, foundation underpinning Australian house prices: there's barely enough supply to meet demand, and the increasing cost of labour and supplies is crimping new homebuilding. All bets are off if a recession hits and unemployment shoots up from its current 4.5% rate. Absent that, resilient bank valuations are putting the lie to a housing disaster Down Under. Follow Antony Currie on Bluesky and LinkedIn .

item.title: ラトニック米商務長官に称賛と非難、米カナダ貿易交渉で土壇場の介入
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 米国とカナダの貿易交渉は、ラトニック米商務長官が土壇場でカナダに圧力をかけた後、決裂した。トランプ米大統領は新たな関税を発動し、カナダのカーニー首相は報復を表明している。

両国が本格的な貿易戦争に突入しつつある中、最終局面でラトニック氏が果たした役割に注目が集まっている。同氏は枠組み合意について、カナダに寛大過ぎると判断。譲歩の撤回を求めていた米金属メーカーの代弁者として前面に出た。非公開の交渉内容だとして、事情に詳しい関係者が匿名を条件に語った。

一部の関係者によると、カナダ側はラトニック氏が交渉条件を後から変えたとして非難。一方、米国側の一部企業幹部は、トランプ氏が保護を約束する米金属業界への脅威になりかねない合意を阻止したとして同氏を評価している。

トランプ氏は先週18日、カナダとの通商合意が近いと発表し、幅広いカナダ製品に対する50%の関税発動を延期した。ただ、グリア米通商代表部（USTR）代表が数週間にわたるカナダとの交渉でまとめた枠組みについて、ラトニック氏と関税強硬派のナバロ上級顧問は批判しており、既に対立の構図が生じていた。

ラトニック氏が今回土壇場で介入し、交渉に深く関与したことで、同氏がトランプ政権内でしばしば波乱を引き起こす人物であることが改めて浮き彫りになった。これまでも、米国がさらに優位に立てると判断した通商案件には、積極的に関与してきた。

ラトニック氏は昨年、自動車や鉄鋼への関税を巡る発言をたびたび変え、市場のボラティリティーを高めていた。取りまとめに関与した日本や韓国との合意では、両国が関税軽減と引き換えに数千億ドル規模の投資を約束したが、当初は慎重な受け止めが広がり、その後も合意を巡る疑問が残っている。ただ、大型案件の一部は発表されている。

米当局者は、行き詰まりの責任はカナダ側にあるとしている。ナバロ氏は「USTRは見事な交渉をした。カナダが合意を受け入れなかったのは非常に愚かだった」と指摘。「条件が良くなることはない。カーニー氏はカナダ国民より政治を選んだ」と述べた。

item.title: ビットコインの人気復活、8万ドル回復－通貨価値希薄化を見込む取引
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 暗号資産（仮想通貨）ビットコインはアジア時間25日の取引で、5月中旬以来となる8万ドル台に値上がりした。長らく低迷してきた暗号資産市場では、強気のシグナルが重なり楽観論が戻りつつある。

ビットコインは一時2.9%高の8万1257ドルと、5月15日以来の高値を付けた。今月23日までの7日間では23%上昇し、週間上昇率として約3年ぶりの大きさとなった。ただ、依然として昨年10月に付けた約12万6000ドルの最高値を大きく下回っている。

ビットコインの人気が復活している。ビットゲット・ウォレットのリサーチアナリスト、レイシー・ジャン氏は、「米財務省が長期債の買い戻し計画を拡大したことでドル安が進み、ビットコインと金で通貨価値の希薄化を見込む取引が再び活発になった。これを受け、マクロ経済環境が一段と追い風になった」と述べた。

ベッセント米財務長官が先週、長期金利の引き下げを目指して米国債の買い戻しを拡大すると発表したことで、通貨価値の希薄化を見込む取引を巡る議論が再燃し、新たなドル売りを誘った。

懐疑派はこの計画について、トランプ政権が財政赤字削減という困難な課題に本格的に取り組む準備がまだできていないことを示すさらなる証拠とみている。

ビットコインはもともと、法定通貨の価値希薄化や中央銀行による通貨供給の拡大がもたらすインフレから逃れる手段として生み出された。

ビットコイン価格の急騰を背景に、ビットコイン現物の上場投資信託（ETF）は先週、週間ベースで10カ月ぶりの大幅な資金流入を記録した。

ブルームバーグがまとめたデータによると、米上場の13本に19億2000万ドル（約3060億円）が純流入し、昨年10月前半以来の高水準を記録。今月20日には6億630万ドルが流入し、1日当たりで3カ月余りで最大となった。

原題：Bitcoin Tops $80,000 on Debasement Trade, Sets Three-Month High （抜粋）

item.title: MLB roundup: Cal Raleigh's 3 HRs help M's end Phils' 9-game win streak
item.description: Cal Raleigh became the first Seattle Mariners player to hit three home runs in a game at T-Mobile Park, giving the hosts a 9-2 victory against the Philadelphia Phillies on Monday night.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Cal Raleigh became the first Seattle Mariners player to hit three home runs in a game at T-Mobile Park, giving the hosts a 9-2 victory against the Philadelphia Phillies on Monday night. The last Seattle player to hit three homers at home was Hall of Famer Edgar Martinez, who did so May 18, 1999, at the Kingdome. The team moved across the street into its new stadium later that summer. Julio Rodriguez and Cole Young also went deep for the Mariners, who won for the third time in four games. Logan Gilbert (11-7) permitted two runs on five hits in five innings. J.T. Realmuto homered for the Phillies, who had a nine-game winning streak snapped. Zack Wheeler (10-5) was tagged for eight runs on nine hits in four-plus innings. Red Sox 4, Marlins 2 Anthony Seigler hit a go-ahead triple in the top of the ninth inning as visiting Boston rallied to defeat Miami for its fourth straight win. In a game in which "Let's go Red Sox" chants could be heard into the ninth inning, Aroldis Chapman pitched a scoreless ninth to earn his 30th save. The Red Sox threw out two Marlins runners at the plate, on throws by first baseman Willson Contreras in the seventh and by reliever Erik Miller (3-0) in the eighth. Miami starter Sandy Alcantara recorded his sixth straight quality start, going seven innings and allowing just one run, but he did not factor into the decision. Otto Lopez had two hits and an RBI. Guardians 4, Angels 2 Austin Hedges slammed a two-run homer and Parker Messick went six strong innings to lead Cleveland past host Los Angeles in Anaheim, Calif. Steven Kwan had two hits and scored a run for the Guardians, who have won five in a row. Messick (10-8) allowed one run on three hits. Angels starter George Klassen (2-2) gave up three runs (two earned) and six hits in 5 1/3 innings. Josh Lowe had two hits for Los Angeles, which has lost three of four. Twins 9, Athletics 6 Ryan Kreidler homered and Zebby Matthews tossed seven innings of one-run ball as Minnesota opened a three-game series against the Athletics with a win in West Sacramento, Calif. Josh Bell drove in three runs and Kaelen Culpepper had a career-high four hits for the Twins, who tallied 16 hits and snapped a three-game losing streak. Byron Buxton added three hits and four runs. The Athletics trailed 9-2 before scoring four runs with two outs in the ninth before Andrew Morris replaced Yoendrys Gomez on the mound and retired Tommy White for his fourth save. Matthews (8-8) won his fourth straight start. Cubs 7, Diamondbacks 0 Michael Conforto and Carson Kelly hit back-to-back homers in a three-run sixth, Kevin Gausman threw seven scoreless innings, and Chicago beat Arizona in Phoenix. Conforto, who also doubled and singled, has homered in two straight games. The Cubs have 12 homers in the past four games. Gausman (7-11) gave up three hits, all singles. Ian Happ and rookie Pedro Ramirez each had two hits and an RBI for the Cubs, who have won two straight. Arizona starter Merrill Kelly (8-12) allowed three runs and five hits in 5 2/3 innings. Pirates 3, Padres 2 (12 innings) Nick Gonzales' RBI single in the top of the 12th inning lifted visiting Pittsburgh to a win over San Diego. Gonzales' bouncer up the middle scored Jared Triolo, the automatic runner at second. The hit made a winner of Kirby Yates (2-5), who escaped a one-out bases-loaded situation in the 11th, and hung a loss on Jeremiah Estrada (2-3). The Pirates ended a three-game skid while stopping the Padres' three-game winning streak. Pittsburgh's Braxton Ashcraft worked six innings, allowing four hits and a run. San Diego's Robbie Ray permitted five hits and two runs in 5 1/3 innings. Giants 5, Reds 0 Rafael Devers blasted a three-run home run and five San Francisco relievers shined after injured starter Carson Whisenhunt exited, completing a five-hitter as the Giants blanked visiting Cincinnati. Drew Gilbert doubled twice and scored a pair of runs for the Giants, who snapped a four-game losing streak. Whisenhunt left in the third inning due to forearm pain. Jason Foley (1-1) fanned three of the four batters he faced for the win. Reds ace Chase Burns (14-3) lasted 3 2/3 innings and allowed season-high-tying totals of five runs and nine hits. Tyler Stephenson collected two hits as Cincinnati lost for the third time in four outings on a nine-game trip. Rays 4, Tigers 1 Jonathan Aranda drove in two runs, including a solo homer, and Drew Rasmussen pitched six strong innings as Tampa Bay beat host Detroit, handing the Tigers their sixth straight loss. Rasmussen (14-5) won his seventh consecutive start since the All-Star break, limiting the Tigers to one run and three hits while striking out five. Garrett Cleavinger, Manuel Rodriguez and Bryan Baker each tossed an inning of scoreless relief, with Baker recording his 38th save. Chandler Simpson had two hits and drove in a run for the Rays, who extended their lead in the American League East to 3 1/2 games over the idle New York Yankees. Framber Valdez (8-9) gave up all four Tampa Bay runs, three earned, on eight hits in six innings and failed to record a strikeout. Nationals 13, Rockies 3 Daylen Lile had three hits, including a three-run homer, and five RBIs, Cade Cavalli turned in six solid innings and host Washington snapped a four-game losing streak with a rout of Colorado. Jorbit Vivas had three hits and drove in two runs for the Nationals, who had lost eight of nine. Cavalli (12-5) gave up two runs on five hits. He struck out seven and walked one. Cavalli has given up three earned runs or fewer in 14 consecutive starts. Willi Castro and Ezequiel Tovar homered for the Rockies, who have lost seven straight. Rockies starter Ryan Feltner (5-8) gave up seven runs (five earned) on six hits over 5 2/3 innings. He struck out six and walked four. Rangers 11, White Sox 2 Corey Seager went 3-for-4 with three RBIs and Jake Burger and Wyatt Langford each homered while collecting two hits and two RBIs, boosting visiting Texas to a victory against Chicago. Kumar Rocker pitched effectively into the sixth inning as the Rangers romped past the American League Central-leading White Sox to take a half-game lead on the idle Houston Astros atop the AL West. Texas scored in five of its first six times at bat, providing ample support for Rocker, who picked up his first victory since July 27. Rocker (5-10) spaced two runs and five hits in 5 2/3 innings. Tristan Peters reached Rocker for a two-run homer in the bottom of the second to pull the White Sox within 3-2. Chicago right-hander Jose Urquidy (2-2) yielded five runs and six hits in three innings with two hit batters. --Field Level Media

item.title: 台風18号、奄美・沖縄に強い勢力で接近へ－空の便に欠航広がる
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 強い台風18号は25日、大東島地方を暴風域に巻き込みながら西北西に進んでいる。同日夜から26日朝にかけて奄美地方と沖縄本島地方に強い勢力で接近する見通しで、航空各社では欠航などの影響が広がっている。

気象庁によると、台風18号は午前10時時点で南大東島の北北西約50キロを時速約20キロで西北西に進んでいる。中心気圧は950ヘクトパスカル、最大風速は毎秒40メートル、最大瞬間風速は同60メートル。中心から半径165キロ以内が風速25メートル以上の暴風域となっている。強い勢力を維持したまま奄美、沖縄本島地方に接近した後、28日ごろにかけて東シナ海を西寄りに進む見込み。

気象庁は奄美地方で26日に土砂災害への厳重な警戒を求めている。奄美、沖縄両地方については27日にかけて、低地の浸水や河川の増水、高潮のほか、落雷や竜巻などの激しい突風にも注意・警戒するよう呼び掛けている。

航空便への影響も拡大している。全日本空輸（ANA）は25日午前11時20分時点で、同日午後の那覇空港発着便の一部について欠航を決定。26日は那覇発着の全便を欠航とするほか、宮古、石垣両空港でも一部便を欠航する。27日も那覇、宮古、石垣の各空港で一部便に影響が出るとしている。

日本航空（JAL）も25日は奄美大島や那覇などを発着する一部便に影響が出ている。北大東、南大東の両空港は同日、終日閉鎖が決まっている。26日はさらに宮古、多良間、石垣、与那国などにも影響範囲が広がる。27日は宮古、多良間、石垣、与那国の発着便に影響が見込まれている。

item.title: ベッセント財務長官の米長期債買い戻し計画、かつてのメンターが論難
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
